primary_external_source.authors: Galyna Livshyts; Grigoris Paouris; Peter Pivovarov
primary_external_source.title: On sharp bounds for marginal densities of product measures
primary_external_source.used_fact: cap-one product law: every k-dimensional orthogonal marginal has density at most 2^(k/2); k=1 gives sqrt(2)

partner_applied.actual_application: scaled to independent marginals with caps M1,M2, yielding pi*M1*M2/sqrt(|det B|)

mathematical_change.statement: For disjoint physical banks I,J,K, if all dependence on I,J factors through independent projections Y=<u,X_I>, Z=<v,X_J> and their 2x2 quadratic matrix B is definite, then ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2*pi/sqrt(|det B|); one singleton bank improves sqrt(2) factor; diagonal B also gives a continuous representative.
mathematical_change.concrete_application: For A_m=[1] direct_sum J_m/m direct_sum (-J_m/m), ||p_Q||_infinity <= pi*sqrt(2) for arbitrary independent cap-one inputs, with continuous density.

unpaid_implication: From only three eigenvalues with absolute value at least one, derive an exhaustive product-preserving bank/diffuse/cross aggregation; current two-bank factorization is not forced by the spectral hypothesis.
